gen-gf-fira-mono-fs-merriweather-sans: Typewriter precision with gaps to spare. Merriweather Sans is the sturdier half, its tall lowercase making each word look large and settled beside the monospace heading.
gen-gf-fira-mono-fs-supreme: Structured, see-through, a bit like a blueprint. If Fira Mono were shrunk down, its wide channels would thin out, while the heavy strip of Supreme sans-serif text keeps its letters held open.
gen-gf-fira-mono-manrope: Fira Mono leads with blocky, spaced-out words and little stroke swing. Manrope, a plain sans in comparison, counters with bright openings at every curve and a pen line that never changes width.
gen-gf-fira-mono-satoshi: Precise from the first glance, Fira Mono sets rigid, see-through letters over Satoshi's soaring x-height. And that tension is the draw: a structured heading against a body whose wide-open e never looks squeezed.
gen-gf-fjalla-one-fs-karma: Tight, compact capitals up top. Fjalla One packs its letters close with slit-like openings, and Karma, a text serif, lets its terminals finish clear of the stem with gentle thinning at the curves.
gen-gf-fragment-mono-fs-merriweather-san: Fragment Mono sets typewriter-like letters with short ascenders and rounded stroke ends, all precise and technical. Merriweather Sans, a plain sans, brings the sturdy, tall-lowercase weight.
gen-gf-fragment-mono-fs-supreme: Single-weight lines, as if drawn by a plotter pen, give Fragment Mono its technical edge. Supreme sans then adds a thick, heavy-looking strip of text beneath, with its letters held open rather than curled shut.
gen-gf-fragment-mono-manrope: Fragment Mono types out its words like a typewriter, with gaping curves and short ascenders. Manrope, a plain sans, takes the other job: bright open curve mouths and a pen line of one width throughout, which feels approachable.
gen-gf-fragment-mono-satoshi: Approachable is Satoshi's mood, with a soaring x-height and a wide-open e, while Fragment Mono brings typewriter-like even-width letters up top. One is rigid and exact; the plain sans flows.
gen-gf-francois-one-fs-erode: Big, bold lowercase with barely a gap in the curves. Erode, a classic serif, counters that with a tall middle band, broad apertures and a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight, which is the pair's sharpest contrast.
